Update on Fish and Wood stories

By: Anina Peens | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Drastic change comes after Carte Blanche exposes the Vanderkloof Rhodes rural fishing project and government takes action against illegal loggers in the Magaliesberg biosphere in the North West provin

Unique Selling Point:
After Carte Blanche did an expose on the Rhodes Rural fishing project at the Vanderkloof dam, the university distances itself from its own project and all attention on wood cutters in the Magaliesberg mountain range in the north West province after police clamp down on illegal activities

Summary:
The Rhodes rural fisheries project at the Vanderkloof dam in the North West province has been called to a halt. This comes after Rhodes university revoked the ethical clearance certificate the project needs to be in operation. After Carte Blanche exposed the story, the university had to save its image. Meanwhile, police and local government have illegal wood poachers in the Magaliesberg mountain range in a tight grip. This also comes after Carte Blanche reported on the loggers, illegally chopping up indigenous trees in the Magaliesberg mountain range to sell as cheap firewood by road vendors.

Further information:
Rhodes University has revoked the ethical clearance certification that was awarded to the Rhodes rural fishing project at the Vanderkloof dam in the Northern Cape province. This comes after various complaints were laid against the project for failing to fulfil on its mandate. The national department of environmental affairs mandated the ichthyology and fisheries department at Rhodes University, to research the viability of a commercial fisheries at the Vanderkloof dam. This was to be done in order for the state to explore possible solutions for poverty alleviation in the province. If the project could prove that a commercial fisheries was viable at the dam, the project would have been used by the state as blue print to role out similar projects countrywide.
But after operating on the dam for longer than two years, and catching tons of fish for the so-called research, the project was stopped. the local fishermen who were to benefit from the project, complained that they were not consulted in any decisions taken by project leaders and that project leaders acting on behalf of Rhodes University only had their own interest at heart. The project leaders could not provide Carte Blanche with any research data collected in the two year period. Further to this, angling societies countrywide were concerned over the project's use of gill nets in the dam, against the better advice given by scientists against the use of gill nets in a dam where protected species occur. The focus was on the Large Mouth Yellow fish.
Rhodes University did not agree to any interviews. a Week after the Carte Blanche expose, the project was halted.

Another story was in the spotlight after CB reported on it. This time, it was illegal wood cutters the Magaliesberg mountain range between Pretoria and Rustenburg. Illegal loggers are chopping indigenous trees in the Magaliesberg which is a UNESCO world heritage site. The wood is then sold as cheap fire wood by illegal vendors next to the road. a Further problem in the area is also the use of gill nets in the Hartbeespoort Dam, that is deemed illegal. a Clamp down that was planned on the illegal fishers spanned out to an simultaneous investigation into the illegal wood vendors at Pelindaba crossing. Local government took wood samples from the vendors at the crossing to determine which wood species are sources from the Magaliesberg. The provincial SAPS says this information will assist them the making arrests in order to ensure that they have solid evidence when prosecuting the perpetrators.

UPDATE
FISH AND WOOD

VO

At the Vanderkloof dam in the Northern Cape, the government had mandated the fisheries science department at Rhodes University to study the viability of establishing a commercial fishery at the dam, to alleviate poverty and uplift and train the local fishing community.

But poverty-stricken local fishermen told us that the inception of the project in 2018 did nothing to uplift them

UPSOUND
SUPER@ LORENZO DAMSTER, FISHERMAN
BUG: SEPTEMBER 2020 CARTE BLANCE

They said that Rhodes University failed to involve them in decisions taken on their behalf.

UPSOUND
SUPER@ LORENZO DAMSTER, FISHERMAN
BUG: SEPTEMBER 2020 CARTE BLANCE

At the time of our investigation, the university would not show us any research data that the project had collected in two years.


After our broadcast, Rhodes University launched an investigation into allegations against the project. We have been reliably informed that the university revoked the ethical clearance for the project.
Ethical clearance is required when research data is collected on behalf of a university and withdrawal of the clearance means that the application of the research for expanding a commercial fishery on the dam… hangs in the balance

INSERT CARTE BLANCHE BUMPER

Meanwhile, days after our broadcast of the problem with illegal wood logging in the Magaliesberg mountains in the North West province, police and government launched an investigation. Illegal wood loggers are chopping down indigenous trees in the mountain which are then sold as cheap firewood.
The Magaliesberg mountains are one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world and is a protected UNESCO world heritage site. Chopping indigenous trees in the mountain is the same as removing or damaging plants in a botanical garden.

SUPER@ JOHN POWERS, ECOLOGIST, NORTH WEST PROVINCIAL GOVERNMENT
ZOOM2’55”
I think just to be aware, the Magaliesberg protected environment is a different category to a normal nature reserve that we know like Pilanesberg. It is protected environment, which that landowners have control means that a lot of it is actually up to the landowners….
BACK-TO-BACK
3’23”
Many of the plants are not actually protected, so it is really the habitat that needs to be protected, and it is really challenging for us to do something.

VO
But this has not stopped government from acting to find solutions.

SUPER@ JOHN POWERS, DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL AFFAIRS
ZOOM 0’40”
“We changed our tactic a little bit this time. Previously it was just a mass confiscation off all wood being sold. This time it was a selective for proper species identification later on… the concern is the mountain, and they are actually cutting there, but I don’t think all the wood is actually from the mountain it could be that some of the wood if from other areas. One has got to be careful of mass confiscations.”

VO
Although the Pelindaba crossing linking the Gauteng and North West Provinces is the biggest depot of firewood sold by street vendors, hundreds of other vendors sell illegal wood next to the road.

SUPER@ SUPER@ JOHN POWERS, DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL AFFAIRS
3’30”
“There needs to be a strong management plan. There needs to be rangers employed in the Magaliesberg to actually to protect the whole range…. But there are initiatives going forward and we do have support from SAPS…we need to work with them. They won’t just independently go and do something, they are more comfortable when we are with them”

VO
The provincial police says it is now waiting for the test results of the wood samples taken in order to plan further raids on illegal wood vendors.

SUPER@ SUPER@BRIG MOKGWABONE, NORTH WEST SAPS
ZOOM 2’27”
“It is good because going forward we know what it is that we need to look out for in order for us to say that they are actually cutting wood that are protected….2’54” We are working together with them… and we are going to work together with the department going forward”
